tickets.title: Live rail enforcement in the scheduler — wire the plugin's PreToolUse hook into every worktree, replace post-hoc glob diff with adlc rails-guard
tickets.body:
handoff.md (this repo, root) is the authoritative design for this ticket. Read it in full before starting — do not re-derive the target integration model, gap analysis, or sequencing. Treat its numbered tasks and acceptance criteria as the contract; this ticket body summarizes and adds verification commands, it does not replace it. Implements handoff.md §5 Workstream B.

PROBLEM: lib/scheduler.mjs only discovers a rail violation after a builder has finished and its full diff is available — the builder has already spent its quota, and shell writes aren't even caught by the in-session hook, only by the CI gate. Booster's worktree-per-ticket model is exactly the shape the plugin's hook was designed for.

RESOLVED AMBIGUITY (coldstart audit, this session): "ensure agy inside that worktree has the plugin active" does NOT mean per-worktree plugin installation. agy plugin installs are user-level (~/.gemini, per handoff.md §2.2's own table describing how booster's current bootstrap vendors skills) and every worktree spawned by the scheduler shares the same $HOME as the parent process — a single global install performed once by T-A's bootstrap already covers every worktree. What genuinely IS per-worktree/per-build is the STATE the hook reads: ADLC_P4_ENFORCEMENT, ADLC_TICKET (or .adlc/current-ticket.json), and the target repo's own .adlc/tickets.json. "Ensure the plugin is active" in task 1 means: verify (not reinstall) the global plugin presence, then set the per-worktree env/state before invoking agy --print in that worktree's cwd. Do not add per-worktree plugin provisioning code — that would be solving a problem that doesn't exist.

TASKS:
1. When runPlan (lib/scheduler.mjs) creates a worktree for a ticket (lib/worktrees.mjs), verify the adlc-antigravity plugin is present (agy plugin list) and set ADLC_P4_ENFORCEMENT=1 for the duration of the builder's agy --print invocation in that worktree, with ADLC_TICKET (or .adlc/current-ticket.json) pointing at the ticket currently being built. This requires the target repo to be ADLC-initialized (.adlc/ present) — if it is not, see task 4.
2. Use lib/adlc-bridge.mjs's planTicketToAdlcTicket (landed in T-C) to materialize the current ticket into the plugin's expected shape before setting ADLC_TICKET. Do not invent new fields.
3. Keep the existing post-hoc scope/rail diff check in scheduler.mjs as the fast-fail confirmation (belt to the hook's suspenders), but change it to call `adlc rails-guard` (diff-based) directly instead of the current bespoke @adlc/core glob comparison, so booster and the plugin share one enforcement engine.
4. When enforcement is unavailable (target repo isn't ADLC-initialized, or adlc/plugin isn't present), booster must fail closed and say so in the ticket log — not silently degrade to prompt-only discipline.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- AC1: A planted rail violation (builder prompt instructed to edit a frozen rail path) is denied during the build, not just failed after. VERIFY: live smoke ticket mirroring the plugin's own "Write to a frozen rail → DENIED" verification; assert the builder's edit attempt is denied and the ticket log shows the denial, not a post-hoc failure.
- AC2: The post-hoc check calls adlc rails-guard. VERIFY: a test that stubs the CLI invocation and asserts it's invoked with the correct diff/base-ref args.
- AC3: Running the scheduler against a non-ADLC-initialized target repo produces a clear warning in the run report, not silent success. VERIFY: run the scheduler against a fixture repo with no .adlc/, assert the run report contains an explicit enforcement-unavailable warning.

edges.contract: lib/scheduler.mjs: B lands rail-enforcement wiring before F3 replaces the two-strike trigger in the same file

tickets.title: Evidence-backed prosecution — wire adlc hollow-test / behavior-diff into lib/prosecute.mjs as hard preconditions
tickets.body:
handoff.md (this repo, root) is the authoritative design for this ticket. Read it in full before starting — do not re-derive the target integration model, gap analysis, or sequencing. Treat its numbered tasks and acceptance criteria as the contract; this ticket body summarizes and adds verification commands, it does not replace it. Implements handoff.md §5 Workstream D.

PROBLEM: lib/prosecute.mjs asks a model to self-report a verdict. The plugin's prosecutor agent instead runs machine-checkable gates (adlc hollow-test, adlc behavior-diff) and backs its verdict with their output. Booster's current approach is exactly the "tests that pass without testing anything" failure mode applied to the reviewer itself.

TASKS:
1. Before dispatching the cross-model prosecution prompt in lib/prosecute.mjs, run `adlc hollow-test --test-cmd "<ticket's gate command>"` against the ticket's worktree. Attach its structured result (survivors, if any) to the prosecution prompt as evidence the model must address.
2. If adlc hollow-test reports exit 2 (mutation survivors), treat this as an automatic prosecution hit (reject) independent of the model's verdict — do not let the model overrule a hard mutation-testing signal.
3. Where the ticket's change touches an HTTP/API surface, run adlc behavior-diff and attach the snapshot comparison the same way.
4. Keep the existing cross-model dispatch (Gemini⇄Claude family alternation) — the CLI gates are additive evidence, not a replacement for cross-model review.
5. Record every prosecution's gate evidence via adlc gate-manifest (coordinate with T-F5 if it has landed; if not, note the manifest call as a TODO hook point, do not block this ticket on F5).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- AC1: A ticket whose tests pass but whose mutation-tested lines survive is rejected even if the LLM verdict says "ship". VERIFY: planted-hollow-test fixture (a test that asserts nothing meaningful about a changed line), run prosecute against it, assert the verdict is reject and cites the hollow-test evidence.
- AC2: Prosecution prompts in the log show the hollow-test evidence block, not just the diff. VERIFY: inspect the generated prompt text in a test, assert it contains the hollow-test result section.
- AC3: Existing cross-model prosecution tests still pass; new tests cover the hard-reject-on-survivors path. VERIFY: npm test exits 0.

edges.contract: lib/prosecute.mjs: D lands hollow-test/behavior-diff wiring before F5 adds gate-manifest recording touching the same file

tickets.title: Booster dogfoods the ADLC on itself — .adlc/ workspace, frozen rails, CI rails-guard, real build/test gate
tickets.body:
handoff.md (this repo, root) is the authoritative design for this ticket. Read it in full before starting — do not re-derive the target integration model, gap analysis, or sequencing. Treat its numbered tasks and acceptance criteria as the contract; this ticket body summarizes and adds verification commands, it does not replace it. Implements handoff.md §5 Workstream E.

PROBLEM: Booster asks every target repo it orchestrates to be ADLC-shaped but is not itself ADLC-initialized. This is a credibility gap as much as a technical one.

NOTE: this repo's .adlc/ workspace and .gitignore stanza (.adlc/* tracked exception !.adlc/tickets.json) were already scaffolded via /adlc-init earlier in this session — task 1 is largely done; verify it, don't redo it blindly.

TASKS:
1. Verify .adlc/ scaffold and .gitignore stanza (done this session) match the plugin's own convention.
2. Add .github/workflows/adlc-rails-guard.yml from ../adlc/docs/ci/rails-guard.yml, make it a required check. Read the security limitation in that template first — it does not protect rails introduced for the first time in the same PR; freeze any new rails in a merged commit before the PR that needs them protected.
3. RESOLVED AMBIGUITY (coldstart audit, this session): enabling GitHub branch-protection rules (required reviewers, required status checks) is a repo-admin action outside a coding agent's reach — it happens in GitHub repo settings or via `gh api` with admin scope, not in a git diff a PR can carry. This ticket's code deliverable is limited to: add a CODEOWNERS file listing the repo owner (derive from `git remote -v` / `gh repo view --json owner`, e.g. the GitHub org/user this repo pushes to) as owner of .github/workflows/**, and add a section to docs/guidelines.md titled "CI self-protection (manual step)" documenting that a human with repo admin access must additionally enable "Require review from Code Owners" in branch protection settings for this to be enforced — link the exact GitHub Settings > Branches path. Do not attempt to call the GitHub API to change branch protection settings as part of this ticket's automated work.
4. Decide and freeze booster's own rails: lib/lock.mjs (merge-lock correctness, hardened over 7 adversarial-review rounds — regressions here are the highest-blast-radius bug class in this repo), lib/gates.mjs (sandbox enforcement), and handoff.md itself once this ticket set is authored (prevents silent scope drift mid-execution). Add these as a ticket's declared "rails" going forward (this ticket set — .adlc/tickets.json — already exists as of this session; a follow-up entry should declare these paths as rails for future tickets touching adjacent files).
5. Add agb's own build/test to CI (currently only publish.yml exists). Gate on the existing 74 unit/integration tests (`npm test`) — this is the prerequisite for the rails-guard CI gate to mean anything; a rails-clean PR that doesn't build is not "safe."

EXPLICITLY DEFERRED (not silently dropped — noted here per handoff.md §5 Workstream F items 7-8): adlc lesson-foundry / rejection-mining (needs volume from gate-manifest history to pay off) and adlc skill-rot (applies to the plugin's doctrine skills once T-A lands, not to booster's own files) are out of scope for this ticket and not ticketed elsewhere in this pass.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- AC1: .adlc/ exists in this repo with ADLC_P4_ENFORCEMENT documented in docs/guidelines.md. VERIFY: file exists; grep docs/guidelines.md for ADLC_P4_ENFORCEMENT.
- AC2: A PR that edits a frozen rail (e.g. lib/lock.mjs without going through the documented ticket process) fails CI. VERIFY: open a scratch PR/branch editing lib/lock.mjs outside ticket scope, confirm the rails-guard workflow run fails.
- AC3: .github/workflows/ includes a real test/build gate, not just publish. VERIFY: workflow file exists and runs `npm test`; a PR with a failing test shows a red check.
- AC4: CODEOWNERS exists and names an owner for .github/workflows/**; docs/guidelines.md has a "CI self-protection (manual step)" section naming the required manual branch-protection step. VERIFY: grep both files for the expected content; this ticket does not call the GitHub API to enable branch protection itself.

edges.contract: docs/guidelines.md: E lands its section before F1 adds the model-router section

tickets.title: [Workstream F] Replace two-strike regeneration trigger with adlc flail-detector
tickets.body:
handoff.md (this repo, root) is the authoritative design for this ticket. Read it in full before starting — do not re-derive the target integration model, gap analysis, or sequencing. Treat its numbered tasks and acceptance criteria as the contract; this ticket body summarizes and adds verification commands, it does not replace it. Implements handoff.md §5 Workstream F, task 3.

Booster's bespoke "two-strike regeneration" trigger (a failed-gate counter) in lib/scheduler.mjs should be replaced with adlc flail-detector's principled detection of repeated errors, scope violations, edit churn, and oversized logs.

COORDINATION NOTE: this ticket touches lib/scheduler.mjs, the same file T-B modifies. Land after T-B merges to avoid a large merge conflict; this is a sequencing note, not a DAG edge, since flail-detector and rail-enforcement wiring touch different functions in the same file.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- AC1: The two-strike counter is replaced (or backed) by adlc flail-detector's signal on the builder's log. VERIFY: a test feeds a fixture log with repeated errors/scope violations to flail-detector and asserts the scheduler's regeneration trigger fires on its verdict, not just a raw failure count.
- AC2: A false-trigger fixture (single transient failure, no flail pattern) does NOT trigger regeneration. VERIFY: test asserts no regeneration for a one-off failure.
- AC3: npm test exits 0.

edges.contract: lib/scheduler.mjs: F3 lands flail-detector wiring before F4 adds consensus-fix fan-out in the same file

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:

- AC2: If consensus-fix itself fails to converge (no winner), the scheduler falls back to the existing single-attempt path with a logged reason, not a silent hang. VERIFY: test simulates a no-consensus result, asserts fallback behavior and log entry.
- AC3: npm test exits 0.
